content: 1. Struthers H, Kamkuemah M, et al. conducted a cross-sectional analysis to investigate the prevalence of gonococcal and chlamydial infections among men who have sex with men (MSM) in Cape Town, South Africa. The study was published in PLoS ONE in 2015 (Volume 10, Issue 9, Article e0138315). 2. Sanders EJ, Wahome E, Okuku HS, Thiong'o AN, Smith AD, Duncan S, et al. evaluated the World Health Organization (WHO) screening algorithm for presumptive treatment of asymptomatic rectal gonorrhea and chlamydia infections in at-risk MSM in Kenya. This study was published in the journal Sexually Transmitted Infections in 2014 (Volume 90, Issue 2, Pages 94-99). 3. Van der Bij AK, Spaargharen J, Morre SA, Fennema HS, Mindel A, Coutinho RA, et al. conducted a retrospective case-control study to assess the diagnostic and clinical implications of anorectal lymphogranuloma venereum (LGV) in MSM. The findings were published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2006 (Volume 42, Issue 2, Pages 186-194). 4. The QUADAS-2 tool was used to assess the risk of bias in various studies. For example, studies by Mugundu, Quilter, Rebe, Sanders, and Passaro were rated as having a low risk of bias across all domains, while the study by Caracas had an unclear risk in one domain. 5. The World Health Organization (WHO) published guidelines in 2021 for the management of symptomatic sexually transmitted infections (STIs). These guidelines provide evidence-based recommendations for clinical practice. 6. The Joanna Briggs Institute developed a reviewer’s manual for conducting systematic reviews of diagnostic test accuracy, including a critical appraisal checklist. 7. Rutter CM and Gatsonis CA proposed a hierarchical regression approach for meta-analysis of diagnostic test accuracy evaluations, published in Statistics in Medicine in 2001 (Volume 20, Issue 19, Pages 2865-2884). 8. Mugundu PR, Narayanan P, Das A, and Morineau G assessed syndromic management algorithms for diagnosing rectal chlamydia and gonorrhea among MSM attending clinics in two Indian cities. This study was published in Sexually Transmitted Infections in 2013 (Volume 89, Supplement 1). 9. Rebe K, Lewis D, Myer L, de Swardt G, Struthers H, Kamkuemah M, et al. conducted a cross-sectional analysis of gonococcal and chlamydial infections among MSM in Cape Town, South Africa, published in PLoS ONE in 2015 (Volume 10, Issue 9, Article e0138315). 10. Quilter LAS, Obondi E, Kunzweiler C, Okall D, Bailey RC, Djomand G, et al. studied the prevalence and correlates of asymptomatic anorectal gonorrhea and chlamydia infections among MSM in Kisumu, Kenya, and developed a risk score for identifying such infections. This study was published in Sexually Transmitted Infections in 2019 (Volume 95, Issue 3, Pages 201-211). 11. Caracas C, Jalil EM, Garcia ACF, Nazer SC, De Oliveira LP, Veloso V, et al. reported high prevalence rates of chlamydia and gonorrhea and low performance of syndromic management among Brazilian transwomen. The findings were published in AIDS Research and Human Retroviruses in 2018 (Volume 34, Supplement 1, Page 240). 12. Passaro RC, Segura ER, Perez-Brumer A, Cabeza J, Montano SM, Lake JE, et al. emphasized the importance of anatomical site-specific screening for urethral, pharyngeal, and rectal gonorrhea and chlamydia among MSM in Lima, Peru. This study was published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 2018 (Volume 45, Issue 9, Pages 607-614). 13. Quilter L, Obondi E, Kunzweiler C, Okall D, Bailey R, Otieno F, et al. developed an empiric risk score to guide presumptive treatment of asymptomatic anorectal infections in MSM in Kisumu, Kenya. This study was published in Sexually Transmitted Infections in 2017 (Volume 93, Supplement 2, Page A142). 14. Van der Bij AK, Spaargharen J, Morre SA, Fennema HS, Mindel A, Coutinho RA, et al. explored the diagnostic and clinical implications of anorectal lymphogranuloma venereum in MSM through a retrospective case-control study, published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2006 (Volume 42, Issue 2, Pages 186-194). 15. The World Health Organization (WHO) released a 2011 report on the prevention and treatment of HIV and other STIs among MSM and transgender individuals. 16. Barbee LA, Khosropour CM, Dombrowski JC, and Golden MR found that new HIV diagnoses were independently associated with rectal gonorrhea and chlamydia in MSM. This study was published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 2017 (Volume 44, Issue 7, Pages 385-389). 17. Henning T, Butler K, Mitchell J, Ellis S, Deyounks F, Farshy C, et al. developed a rectal STI-HIV coinfection model using Chlamydia trachomatis and SHIVSF162p3. The study was published in Journal of Medical Primatology in 2014 (Volume 43, Issue 3, Pages 135-143). 18. Sanders EJ, Okuku HS, Smith AD, Mwangi MM, Wahome E, Fegan G, et al. reported high HIV-1 incidence, correlates of HIV-1 acquisition, and high viral loads following seroconversion among MSM. This study was published in AIDS in 2013 (Volume 27, Issue 3, Pages 437-446). 19. Chan PA, Robinette A, Montgomery M, Almonte A, Cu-Uvin S, Lonks JR, et al. reviewed extragenital infections caused by Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae. The review was published in Infectious Diseases in Obstetrics and Gynecology in 2016 (Article ID 5758387). 20. Kent CK, Chaw JK, Wong W, Liska S, Gibson S, Hubbard G, et al. investigated the prevalence of rectal, urethral, and pharyngeal chlamydia and gonorrhea in MSM in San Francisco, California, in 2003. The study was published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2005 (Volume 41, Issue 1, Pages 67-74). 21. Soni S and White JA evaluated self-screening for Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia trachomatis in an HIV clinic, reporting high yields and acceptability. This study was published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 2011 (Volume 38, Issue 12, Pages 1107-1109). 22. Turner AN, Reese PC, Ervin M, Davis JA, Fields KS, Bazan JA examined the prevalence of HIV, rectal chlamydia, and rectal gonorrhea in MSM attending an STI clinic in a Midwestern US city. The study was published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 2013 (Volume 40, Issue 6, Pages 433-438). 23. Ross MW, Nyoni J, Ahaneku HO, Mbwambo J, McClelland RS, McCurdy SA reported high HIV seroprevalence, rectal STIs, and risky sexual behavior in MSM in Dar es Salaam and Tanga, Tanzania. The study was published in BMJ Open in 2014 (Volume 4, Issue 8, Article e006175). 24. Kim EJ, Hladik W, Barker J, Lubwama G, Sendagala S, Ssenkusu JM, et al. found associations between alcohol use, HIV infection, and STIs among MSM in Kampala, Uganda. This study was published in Sexually Transmitted Infections in 2016 (Volume 92, Issue 3, Pages 240-245). 25. Muraguri N, Tun W, Okal J, Broz D, Raymond HF, Kellogg T, et al. investigated HIV and STI prevalence and risk factors among male sex workers and other MSM in Nairobi, Kenya. The study was published in Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2015 (Volume 68, Issue 1, Pages 91-96). 26. Katz DA, Dombrowski JC, Bell TR, Kerani RP, Golden MR examined HIV incidence among MSM after diagnosis with STIs. This study was published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 2016 (Volume 43, Issue 4, Pages 249-254). 27. Rowley J, Vander Hoorn S, Korenromp E, Low N, Unemo M, Abu-Raddad LJ, et al. provided global prevalence and incidence estimates for chlamydia, gonorrhea, trichomoniasis, and syphilis in 2016. The findings were published in Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 2019 (Volume 97, Issue 8, Pages 548-562). 28. Van Boeckel TP, Gandra S, Ashok A, Caudron Q, Grenfell BT, Levin SA, et al. analyzed global antibiotic consumption from 2000 to 2010 using national pharmaceutical sales data. This study was published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2014 (Volume 14, Issue 8, Pages 742-750). 29. Ong JJ, Baggaley RC, Wi TE, Tucker JD, Fu H, Smith MK, et al. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on the global epidemiologic characteristics of STIs among individuals using pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) for HIV prevention. The study was published in JAMA Network Open in 2019 (Volume 2, Issue 12, Article e1917134). 30. Okuku HS, Wahome E, Duncan S, Thiongo A, Mwambi J, Shafi J, et al. evaluated presumptive treatment recommendations for asymptomatic anorectal gonorrhea and chlamydia infections in at-risk MSM in Kenya. This study was published in Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2012 (Volume 15, Article 99).
